Cause: The docs-site 4.3 pod spec added `securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` (part of the quarterly hardening — a recommended practice [cite: concepts/security/application-security-checklist#security-context-container-0]). Next.js tries to create its image-optimizer cache at `/app/.next/cache` on startup, which fails on the read-only root filesystem.

Evidence:
- `list_pods` in `marketing` shows the new ReplicaSet pod `docs-site-5c7b9d4f6-wk4pz` running image `docs-site:4.3.0` in CrashLoopBackOff (11 restarts) with `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`; the 4.2.0 pods are healthy and do not have that setting.
- Pod logs show: `Error: EROFS: read-only file system, mkdir '/app/.next/cache'` from `ImageOptimizerCache.init` right after Next.js starts, then exit 1. (The earlier New Relic 401 messages are unrelated — the agent logs the error and continues.)

Fix: Keep `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` and give the container a writable `emptyDir` mounted at the cache path. Add to the Deployment pod spec:

```yaml
volumes:
- name: next-cache
  emptyDir: {}
# in the container:
volumeMounts:
- name: next-cache
  mountPath: /app/.next/cache
```

An `emptyDir` volume is the standard way to provide scratch/cache space to a container [cite: concepts/storage/volumes#emptydir-4]. If the app writes to other paths too (e.g. `/tmp`), mount emptyDirs there as well. After redeploying, the new ReplicaSet should become Ready and the rollout will complete.
